### Dr. Abdullahi Mohamed Mohamud
**National Surveillance Officer, Federal Ministry of Health, Somalia**

> Participating in the ARBO WATCH capacity-building program strengthened my practical skills in disease surveillance data work and research. The training gave me hands-on skills in data collection and management tools (Kobo Toolbox, Google Forms, Excel), introduced me to R for public health surveillance, and deepened my understanding of statistical modelling for epidemiological research. These skills have directly supported how I analyze and interpret surveillance data during outbreak investigation.
>
> I thank the ARBO WATCH consortium and the JKUAT team for this well-structured and practical training to develop epidemiological models for predicting the incidence of dengue and chikungunya and provide decision-support tools to inform surveillance and control in the Horn of Africa.
:::
:::

::: {.g-col-12 .g-col-md-8 .testimonial-content}
### Dr. Ahmed Yusuf
**Public Health Department, Federal Ministry of Health, Somalia**

> The five-module data training program was an exceptional professional development experience. The interactive morning and afternoon practical sessions provided hands-on expertise in essential tools, including advanced Excel for data management, R for statistical analysis, and QGIS for spatial health mapping.
>
> Beyond the technical skills I have acquired, the program allowed me to build a valuable professional network with brilliant colleagues across the field. I am deeply grateful to the organizers and everyone who made this possible, especially the mentors whose dedication, guidance, patience, and interactive support made this training so impactful.
>
> Applying these tools directly to real-world datasets has significantly strengthened my capacity to analyze complex health data, visualize disease trends, and support evidence-based public health policy.
:::
